subject: Provisional latency carveout & temporary uptime waiver for batched inference
messages:
From: Sam Solis <sam.solis@solishealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@solishealth.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA request: latency carveout for batched inference spikes

Irene —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the preliminary load tests against the staging endpoint this morning and saw some consistent P95 latency spikes during our 10–12pm batch window. Those spikes are short (90–120s) but appear every ~15 minutes and coincide with our end-of-day report batching.

This is a concern for our internal SLAs because we commit <200ms p50 / 800ms p95> for patient-facing flows. For the batched analytics jobs we can accept higher tail latency so long as the hosted service provides: 1) a documented temporary carveout for batched traffic, 2) a rollback/notification window so we don’t get surprised by credits, and 3) a capped monthly credit exposure while we tune workload patterns.

Can Redwood propose wording for the SLA template to cover a provisional latency exception for non-customer-facing batches and a monthly cap on remedy credits during the pilot? Procurement is ready to route a PO but they want language before signing. I attached our PO (Solis-procurement-PO-5567.pdf) to speed things up.

—Sam
Sam Solis
Director, Platform Engineering
Solis Health
sam.solis@solishealth.com

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Solis <sam.solis@solishealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA request: latency carveout for batched inference spikes

Sam —

Appreciate the clear summary and the PO — this is helpful. We can definitely accommodate a provisional carveout for explicitly identified "batching" traffic with a few guardrails so the exception doesn't create broad exposure for either party.

High-level proposal (draft language — I'll have legal refine):
- Provisional Batched-Job Latency Exception: For workloads identified in writing as "batching" (e.g., scheduled analytics or bulk report generation), Redwood will not apply standard P95 latency remedies during short-duration batch windows provided the request matches documented traffic markers. The provisional carveout may be active for an initial 90-day pilot period.
- Notification & Rollback: Redwood will provide automated alerts when carveout-eligible windows exceed an agreed frequency or duration threshold. If carveout conditions are exceeded for >3 months or more than 5 unplanned events in a 30-day period, either party may terminate the carveout and normal SLA remedy calculations will resume.
- Monthly Remedy Cap During Pilot: Remedy credits triggered by events occurring within carveout windows will be subject to a capped monthly payment not to exceed USD 25,000 or 10% of the monthly recurring commitment, whichever is lower, for the 90-day pilot.

Attachments: redwood-sla-draft-v2.pdf (proposed clause markup), ops-runbook-batched.xlsx (operational markers to identify batching). Please review. Laura — looping you in for a quick legal sanity check on the remedy cap language. Karthik — can you confirm technical feasibility of the automated alerts + markers (token flags / request header) we referenced?

Next steps: If Solis signs off I can circulate a tracked-change SLA and a short addendum for e-signature.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Sam Solis <sam.solis@solishealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA request: latency carveout for batched inference spikes

Sam / Irene —

Quick technical notes from infra: we can reliably tag batch requests at the edge using a custom header (x-solis-batch: true) or by routing by IP/namespace. The runtime already exposes a per-workload telemetry flag so we can emit an "inside-carveout-window" metric. Alerts: we can push to your PagerDuty or an email hook when per-window P95 exceeds the configured threshold.

Mitigations that reduce the need for an exception (options if you want to avoid a carveout):
- Stagger batch intervals by 3–5 minutes to avoid synchronized spikes
- Use a lower-priority dedicated worker pool for batch jobs (we can allocate a 1-2 GPU pool for scheduled runs during the pilot)
- Apply soft rate-limiting at the scheduler to smooth burst arrivals

Credit math note: if you want the cap tied to usage instead of a fixed USD amount we can propose: Monthly cap = min(USD 25,000, 10% * MRC) OR USD 0.02 * total monthly tokens originating from batch-marked requests (whichever is lower). That keeps the cap proportional to actual impact.

Happy to kick off a 90-day pilot with the opt-in header approach; ops-runbook already documents the metadata we'll use.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Solis <sam.solis@solishealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@solishealth.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA request: latency carveout for batched inference spikes

Thanks — this looks reasonable. Procurement is OK with a 90-day pilot and the roll-back triggers you outlined. Two asks before we sign: 1) bump the temporary monthly cap to USD 30,000 (we’re slightly above the expected MRC during trial), and 2) add a clause that Redwood will provide a monthly summary report of all carveout-window events (timestamp, duration, token count, remedy calculation if any).

If you can accept that I can route the PO and our admin will sign the addendum — I attached the purchase order for reference. We prefer DocuSign for the addendum.

Sam

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Solis <sam.solis@solishealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA request: latency carveout for batched inference spikes

Sam —

We can accept the revised monthly cap of USD 30,000 for the 90-day pilot and will include the monthly carveout event summary in the addendum (standard fields: timestamp, duration, requests, tokens, remedial credit calculation). I asked Legal to add a short audit right (read-only logs) so Solis Health can validate event attribution during the pilot. Laura is on the thread to finalize wording.

I will: 1) circulate the tracked-change SLA addendum for signature via DocuSign; 2) schedule an ops kickoff with Karthik for next Monday (July 5) to validate headers and alert hooks; and 3) attach the final addendum to the HubSpot deal. Expect DocuSign link in the morning.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot started.

Best,
Irene
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
